newsitem.title: USA: New Jersey budget clears committees, passage seen.
newsitem.headline: New Jersey budget clears committees, passage seen.

text.p: A $16.8-billion election-year budget easily cleared the budget committees of both chambers of the New Jersey Legislature Monday, setting the stage for its passage Thursday. It has grown by $400 million since Gov. Christie Whitman introduced it in January.
In a year with all 40 Senate seats and 80 in the Assembly on the Nov. 4 ballot, little opposition is expected.

Among the new spending is $246 million to satisfy the state Supreme Court order to increase state aid to the 28 poorest school districts; $55 million in high tech grants for higher education plus $30 million for college salaries, and $18 million to increase the state's child protection staff.
Two proposals were rejected -- $100 million to pay mostly urban hospitals for charity care and $55 million to fund a child-care tax credit.

The extra spending was made possible by two developments, namely Whitman's plan to sell $2.75 billion in pension bonds, enabling the state to skip $590 million in contributions, and an unanticipated bounty of tax revenue, estimated to exceed budget projections by $500 million.
